priorStories.headline: Grand jury rejects charges against Cassidy Hutchinson
priorStories.body:
A federal grand jury in Washington declined prosecutors’ request to indict former White House aide Cassidy Hutchinson over allegations that she lied to Congress about President Donald Trump’s actions surrounding the January 6, 2021, Capitol attack. The proposed charges have not been made public.

Hutchinson says she stands by her testimony. The Justice Department did not immediately comment.

sources.name: ABC News via ABC7 Los Angeles

priorStories.headline: Israeli exit polls show no majority
priorStories.body:
Voting ended in Israel’s Knesset election, and exit polls from the major television broadcasters projected that neither Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s bloc nor the opposition led by Gadi Eisenkot had won the 61 seats needed for a majority.

Likud was projected to remain the largest party, but official results were still pending. Forming a government could depend on coalition negotiations lasting several weeks.

candidates.summary: A high-speed train struck the rear of another train that had stopped near Urda in Spain’s Toledo province, derailing two cars. Authorities reported at least 64 deaths and about 80 injuries as rescue work continued. The two trains carried more than 500 passengers in total and were traveling from Madrid toward Seville. The cause remained under investigation, and rail service between Madrid, Ciudad Real and Andalusia was suspended.
candidates.title: Spain train collision kills at least 64

candidates.summary: Official returns from Israel’s election continued to show no governing majority. With about 85% of votes counted, Likud had 20.8%, Gadi Eisenkot’s Yashar had 16.1%, and Arab-led parties collectively had 14.9%. Local projections assigned 53 seats to Likud and its allies, 48 to Yashar’s bloc and 19 to Arab-led parties, making the latter potentially decisive in coalition talks. Roughly half a million absentee ballots remained to be counted.
candidates.title: Israeli count leaves Arab-led parties holding potential balance

candidates.summary: The Federal Reserve held its benchmark federal funds rate at 3.75% to 4%, saying economic activity was expanding strongly while inflation remained elevated. The decision passed 10-2. Governor Lisa Cook and Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack favored raising the range by a quarter percentage point.
candidates.title: Federal Reserve holds interest rates steady

candidates.summary: The reported death toll from the collision of two high-speed trains near Urda in Spain’s Toledo province rose to at least 68. Dozens of people were injured after one train struck the rear of another that had stopped, derailing two cars. Authorities continued rescue and investigative work, and rail service on affected routes remained disrupted.
candidates.title: Spain train collision death toll rises to at least 68

candidates.summary: U.S. District Judge David O. Carter denied the Justice Department’s request to stop California from processing ballots from up to 20,000 people whom the federal government alleged were likely noncitizens. Carter said the requested segregation could disenfranchise eligible voters and disrupt an election already underway. The Justice Department said it would appeal.
candidates.title: Judge rejects federal request to segregate California ballots

candidates.summary: Utah filed felony criminal charges against prediction-market operator Kalshi and co-founders Tarek Mansour and Luana Lopes Lara. The charges include 13 counts alleging violations of Utah’s gambling prohibition and one count involving profits from allegedly illegal activity. Kalshi called the prosecution an overreach and said it would challenge the case.
candidates.title: Utah files felony charges against Kalshi and its founders

candidates.summary: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth removed Army Lt. Gen. Brett Sylvia as the Joint Chiefs of Staff’s director for strategy, plans and policy, according to a defense official. No reason or immediate replacement was announced. The Joint Staff thanked Sylvia for his 32 years of service.
candidates.title: Hegseth removes Pentagon’s top military planner

candidates.summary: The Justice Department filed notice that the National Park Service plans to submit a design for renovating Washington’s East Potomac Golf Course and close the course and the portion of the park south of Buckeye Drive by November 15. A preliminary injunction still bars additional tree removal or other irreversible changes without notice while litigation challenging the project continues.
candidates.title: Federal filing confirms East Potomac golf course renovation plan

candidates.summary: The Milwaukee Brewers defeated the Tampa Bay Rays 4-1 in Game 5 to win the first World Series championship in franchise history. Jacob Misiorowski pitched 5 2/3 scoreless innings, while Cooper Pratt recorded two hits and two RBIs. Catcher William Contreras was named World Series MVP.
candidates.title: Milwaukee Brewers win first World Series championship

candidates.summary: New York Gov. Kathy Hochul signed legislation prohibiting specified companion-chatbot behavior when interacting with children under 18, including falsely presenting the chatbot as a real person, providing sexually explicit material, encouraging secrecy or unhealthy conduct, and certain uses of flattery. The law, scheduled to take effect January 1, allows enforcement by the state attorney general.
candidates.title: New York signs restrictions on companion chatbots used by children
